notes: Overturn confirmed, on the EXTEND arm. 'Applicable' is the USE statement's own scope: a procedure applies to a file when the USE rules can invoke it for that file, either by naming it (GR5a) or by an open mode the file can be in (GR5b-e); the I-O status rules use the word the same way ('whether an applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure will be executed', VIII.1.3.4), and GR3 of the invalid key condition requires, with no phrase, that a USE procedure 'must be associated with the file connector and that procedure is executed'. An EXTEND procedure runs only for a file open, or being opened, in extend mode (GR5e), and a file in random or dynamic access can never be (VIII.4.4.3 SR1 / IX.4.4.3 SR1; the compiler itself refuses OPEN EXTEND of such a file, COBOL2372). So for a random- or dynamic-access file a USE ... ON EXTEND is not an applicable procedure, the rule requires the phrase, and the compiler admits the statement: ExceptionPhraseRequirement.HasApplicableUse.Covers returns true for any mode declarative (d.ModeIndex is not null). The access mode is what decides, and the own probe extseq.cob separates the readings: on a SEQUENTIAL-access indexed file opened EXTEND, a WRITE out of key order with no phrase is taken by the USE ON EXTEND procedure (USE EXTEND 21), so there the procedure is applicable and the compiler is right to accept it. The other half of the code's reading (INPUT, OUTPUT and I-O declaratives count for every file: docs/FILES_DESIGN.md D31(a)) is not needed for this verdict; whether a mode the file can be in, but in which the guarded condition cannot arise, is 'applicable' is the open reading held on 1985-SR-IX.4.3.3-2 and is not decided here. This row: indexed RANDOM REWRITE. The phrase requirement is implemented (no phrase and no USE, or a USE on another file, is refused COBOL6826) and the file-name and GLOBAL halves of 'applicable' are right; only the EXTEND declarative is counted for a file it can never cover. The repro's run-time status is 49 (the file is not open I-O), not an invalid key; the rule is a syntax rule and refuses the program whatever the run-time path, so the static evidence (compiles clean) is what decides. Note PB5413 is right in its citations, expected result (COBOL6826) and harm flags (under_rejects, silent). It should add: (1) the same defect for a sequential file with LINAGE, which can never be opened EXTEND (§1985:VII.4.3.3 SR3): own probe linx.cob, a LINAGE file with only USE ... ON EXTEND and a READ with no AT END, compiles at --std 85, so the fix's 'EXTEND only for sequential access' must also exclude LINAGE files, and the row 1985-SR-VII.4.4.3-2 has the same arm; (2) the doc comment of ExceptionPhraseRequirement.HasApplicableUse (ExceptionPhraseRequirement.cs lines 69-73) states the D31(a) claim 'a mode declarative is applicable to every statement of every file it could cover' and must change with docs/FILES_DESIGN.md D31(a) ('A mode declarative covers every statement, because the file may be in any mode', line 2328). Aside: COBOL2372 at --std 85 cites ISO §2023:14.9.27.3 SR2, not §1985:VIII.4.4.3 SR1. kb/Work PB5413 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set7/decisions.json).

next.reason: §1985:IX.4.6.3 SR3, as replaced by X3.23a-1989 (the printed rule also required NOT INVALID KEY): 'The INVALID KEY phrase must be specified in the REWRITE statement for indexed files for which an appropriate USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is not specified'. 2023 has no such syntax rule (§2023:14.9.35.3 SR2 only forbids the phrase for sequential organization and for relative organization in sequential access mode); §2023:14.9.35.4 GR19, under RELATIVE AND INDEXED FILES, makes the transfer of control depend 'on the presence or absence of the optional INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY phrases in the REWRITE statement', and the refused case is stated by §2023:9.1.14 GR4: 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement and there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement'; so too §2023:9.1.14 GR3: 'If control is returned from those statements or there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement'. Words that differ: 1985 'must be specified'; 2023 'not specified ... there are no applicable ... exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end'. A statement 1985 refuses is accepted by 2023 with a stated run-time effect: a lifted refusal, so CHANGED (kb/Work PB5021), not REMOVED.
